title: Advancing Pediatric Growth Assessment with Machine Learning: Overcoming Challenges in Early Diagnosis and Monitoring
content: This article explores the transformative role of machine learning (ML) in pediatric growth assessment, emphasizing the early diagnosis and monitoring of growth disorders. A logistic regression algorithm, developed using R, analyzes biometric and demographic data to identify anomalies in children's growth patterns. The study employs a cross-sectional dataset comprising real- world data from Stanford Medicine Children’s Health and references from reputable sources to model growth variations in children aged 6 to 13. The methodology includes a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to identify key trends, complemented by data preprocessing techniques such as cleaning, normalization, and feature selection to enhance model performance. The results show that logistic regression achieves an accuracy of 94.65% and a sensitivity of 91.03%, significantly improving the accuracy and timeliness of diagnosing growth anomalies compared to traditional methods. The study concludes that ML, particularly logistic regression, offers promising applications in pediatric health by enhancing diagnostic precision and operational efficiency. However, challenges remain related to data quality, clinical integration, and privacy concerns. Future research should focus on improving data diversity, model interpretability, and external validation to support clinical decision- making. The algorithm and related data are available in a GitHub repository to promote transparency, reproducibility, and collaborative development within the scientific community.
